summary.description: 3-5 sentences: what the article argues and what it reveals about forecasting or modeling.

model_content_level.description: How much the article reveals about how election models (Silver's or others) work. none = nothing usable.

models_discussed.description: Models or products discussed, e.g. 'Silver Bulletin 2024 presidential model', 'FLIPR 2026 midterms model', 'Silver Bulletin polling averages', 'Silver Bulletin pollster ratings', 'FiveThirtyEight (Silver era, 2008-2022)', 'FiveThirtyEight (2024, Morris era)', 'Economist model', 'prediction markets'.

findings.description: Every distinct piece of information about how forecasting models are or should be built. One atomic idea per item.

statement.description: Precise, self-contained statement understandable without the article. Name the model, the mechanism, and any numbers.

quantities.description: Every number attached to this finding. Empty array if none.

unit.description: e.g. 'percentage points', 'days', 'simulations'. Empty string if unitless.

context.description: What the number applies to and when.

rationale.description: Why the author does it this way or believes it, as stated or clearly implied. Empty string if none given.

model_version.description: Which model/version/period this applies to, e.g. '2024 presidential', 'FLIPR 2026', '538 2016-2020', 'general principle'.

evidence_quote.description: Short verbatim quote from the article supporting the finding, at most 40 words. Empty string if the finding comes from a chart or table.

explicitness.description: explicit = stated outright; implied = clearly suggested but not spelled out; inferred_from_chart = read off a figure or table.

political_insights.description: Substantive claims about electoral behavior, coalitions, and political dynamics that a forecaster should know, even if not about model mechanics.

topic.description: Short label, e.g. 'incumbency advantage', 'education realignment', 'midterm penalty'.

evidence.description: Data, numbers, or reasoning offered. Empty string if none.

forecasting_implication.description: How a forecaster could use this. Empty string if unclear.

references.description: Methodology pages, papers, datasets, or other articles the text points to that could hold more model detail.

open_questions.description: Model details the article alludes to but does not explain, worth chasing elsewhere.
